title: Comparison chart: Antiviral drugs for seasonal influenza.
abstract: Influenza is typically a self-limited illness, but complications including pneumonia, respiratory failure, and death can occur, especially in persons at increased risk (see Table 1). Influenza vaccination reduces the incidence of laboratory-confirmed influenza and the risk of complications associated with influenza illness. Annual vaccination should be offered to all persons ≥6 months old as long as influenza viruses are circulating in the community.
journal: The Medical letter on drugs and therapeutics

title: Epidemiological Modeling of Seasonal Influenza Through Periodic Mean-Reverting Stochastic Processes
abstract: Seasonal influenza follows annual cycles, but variation in epidemic magnitude and timing complicates preparedness. We applied periodic mean reverting stochastic differential equations (SDEs) to seven seasons of weekly Texas influenza surveillance data. Missing observations were imputed using MissForest and compared with four alternative methods. Stochastic variability was modeled using {sigma}X(t) dW(t), with p = 1/2,2/3,5/6, and 1, representing square root, intermediate sublinear, and multiplicative diffusion. Each specification was evaluated for direct influenza modeling and within a susceptible, exposed, infectious , and recovered model incorporating waning immunity, where the SDE governed transmission. Parameters were estimated using least squares and approximate maximum likelihood for direct models and sample-proportion weighted least squares for stochastic SEIR models. Model-based parametric bootstrap assessed direct-model parameter uncertainty. For direct modeling, p = 1/2 achieved the lowest RMSE (712.8) and AIC (5383.0), with similar AIC for p = 2/3 (5383.2). For stochastic SEIR modeling, p = 1 achieved the lowest RMSE (0.02926), compared with 0.03506 for p = 1/2. The deterministic SEIR model yielded R = 1.158. Transmission peaked approximately 10 weeks before infectious prevalence, while stochastic transmission generated variation in epidemic peak timing. Bootstrap analysis identified dependence between mean-reversion and diffusion parameters. Overall, the appropriate diffusion structure depended on the epidemiological quantity modeled, supporting flexible characterization of seasonal transmission variability while requiring prospective validation before operational forecasting.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to improve preparedness for seasonal influenza by modeling its annual cycles using periodic mean-reverting stochastic differential equations (SDEs). The researchers applied these equations to seven seasons of weekly Texas influenza surveillance data, focusing on the dynamics of transmission and epidemic variability. They imputed missing observations using MissForest and compared them with alternative methods. For direct modeling, the parameter p = 1/2 achieved the lowest RMSE and AIC, suggesting it best captured influenza variability. The study also evaluated the SDEs within a susceptible, exposed, infectious, and recovered (SEIR) model, incorporating waning immunity. The findings highlight the importance of selecting the appropriate diffusion structure based on the epidemiological quantity being modeled, which could enhance understanding of seasonal transmission patterns. However, the study emphasizes the need for prospective validation before operational forecasting. The analysis identified dependence between mean-reversion and diffusion parameters, indicating potential complexities in model interpretation. While the study provides valuable insights into modeling influenza dynamics, its results are based on historical data and may not fully account for real-time variability or external factors influencing transmission.

abstract_zh: 季节性流感具有年度周期性,但疫情规模和时间的变化使准备工作复杂化。我们采用周期性均值回复随机微分方程(SDEs)对德克萨斯州七季的每周流感监测数据进行了分析。使用MissForest填补缺失观测值,并与四种替代方法进行了比较。随机波动性通过{sigma}X(t) dW(t)进行建模,其中p = 1/2,2/3,5/6,和1,分别代表平方根、中间次线性和乘法扩散。每种模型规格均在直接流感建模和一个包含免疫力减弱的易感-暴露-感染-恢复(SEIR)模型中进行了评估,其中SDE控制传播。直接模型的参数估计使用最小二乘法和近似最大似然法,而随机SEIR模型则使用样本比例加权最小二乘法进行估计。基于模型的参数化自引导分析评估了直接模型参数的不确定性。在直接建模中,p = 1/2实现了最低的均方误差(RMSE)(712.8)和AIC(5383.0),而p = 2/3的AIC相近(5383.2)。在随机SEIR建模中,p = 1的RMSE最低(0.02926),相比p = 1/2的0.03506有所改善。确定性SEIR模型得出的R值为1.158。传播的峰值大约比感染患病率早10周,而随机传播则产生了疫情峰值时间的变化。自引导分析识别了均值回复与扩散参数之间的依赖关系。总体而言,合适的扩散结构取决于所建模的流行病学量,这支持了对季节性传播变化的灵活描述,但在操作性预测之前需要进行前瞻性验证。

title: Affinity Peptide-Engineered Magnetic Microswimmers for Ultrafast On-the-Fly Screening of Influenza A Virus in Microliter-Scale Samples.
abstract: Abstract Monitoring respiratory viruses is crucial for mitigating their spread and the associated healthcare costs, especially during the cold season. This study presents an on-the-fly OFF–ON fluorescence approach for the H3N2 subtype of Influenza A virus determination using magnetically propelled WS2/Ni micromotors. The micromotors are modified with a rhodamine B-labeled peptide highly specific toward the hemagglutinin A HA1 protein antigen. The improved fluid mixing imparted by the micromotor motion allows for efficient operation during an assay time of 1 min using just 1 μL of sample. The developed fluorescent assay represents a reliable and robust screening platform for influenza clinical samples, achieving exceptional selectivity and limits of detection in the ng/L range. The method’s performance was validated using nasopharyngeal specimens, demonstrating high reliability and analytical specificity for the Influenza A H3N2 subtype. Notably, the protocol provided high fluorescence signatures for H3N2-infected samples even when cycle threshold (Ct) values were comparable those of to H1N1-infected samples and negative samples. These results highlight the reliability of the proposed micromotor-based strategy for rapid viral subtyping and demonstrate its potential as a fast sample-to-result diagnostic platform requiring minimal sample volume.

abstract_zh: 摘要 监测呼吸道病毒对于减轻其传播和相关的医疗费用至关重要,尤其是在寒冷季节。本研究提出了一种使用磁驱动 WS2/Ni 微电机测定甲型流感病毒 H3N2 亚型的动态 OFF-ON 荧光方法。微电机经过罗丹明 B 标记肽的修饰,该肽对血凝素 A HA1 蛋白抗原具有高度特异性。微电机运动带来的改进的流体混合允许仅使用 1 μL 样品在 1 分钟的测定时间内进行高效操作。开发的荧光检测为流感临床样本提供了可靠且强大的筛选平台,实现了卓越的选择性和 ng/L 范围内的检测限。该方法的性能通过鼻咽标本进行了验证,证明了对甲型 H3N2 流感亚型的高可靠性和分析特异性。值得注意的是,即使循环阈值 (Ct) 值与 H1N1 感染样品和阴性样品相当,该方案也为 H3N2 感染样品提供了高荧光特征。这些结果凸显了所提出的基于微电机的快速病毒分型策略的可靠性,并证明了其作为需要最小样本量的快速样本到结果诊断平台的潜力。

title: Isolation, identification and whole genome sequence analysis of influenza B virus from Shanghai during 2023-2024.
abstract: Influenza B virus, a member of the Orthomyxoviridae family, is a significant contributor to global respiratory infections alongside influenza A virus. This study investigated the prevalence and genomic characteristics of influenza B virus during the 2023-2024 season in Shanghai, China. Among 174 clinical samples collected from the Nanxiang Branch of Ruijin Hospital, the positivity rate for influenza B virus was 62.36%. Genomic analysis revealed that all characterized isolates belonged to the B/Victoria lineage and were classified within subclade C.5.7, corresponding to the legacy designation V1A.3a.2. No B/Yamagata lineage strains were detected. Comparative genomic analysis further revealed close genetic similarity between the Shanghai isolates and strains from Shanxi Province, suggesting a potential geographical or evolutionary relationship. These findings highlight the substantial activity of influenza B virus in Shanghai during the study period and underscore the importance of continued genomic surveillance to monitor viral evolution and inform public health strategies.

title: Antiviral Treatment of Human Influenza A(H5N1) Infection: Treatment Timing, Clinical Outcomes, Virological Outcomes, and Antiviral Resistance: A Systematic Review
abstract: Human influenza A(H5N1) infection remains a clinically important zoonotic disease, but evidence on antiviral effectiveness is limited by observational designs, heterogeneous treatment timing, and potentially overlapping patient populations. This systematic review synthesized evidence on antiviral regimens, treatment timing, clinical and virological outcomes, and antiviral resistance in laboratory-confirmed human A(H5N1) infection. A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and ScienceDirect was conducted from database inception to 1 July 2026. Methodological quality was assessed using the Newcastle–Ottawa Scale and the JBI Case Series Checklist. The clinical and methodological characteristics varied across studies; consequently, the findings were synthesized narratively. Potential population overlap was considered when synthesizing findings across publications to avoid duplicate aggregation of patient data. Of 2,329 records identified, 22 publications were included. Oseltamivir treatment was associated with a lower hazard of death than no documented anti-influenza antiviral treatment (adjusted hazard ratio 0.51, 95% confidence interval 0.34–0.77). Treatment within 2 days showed lower odds of death, although the overall estimate was not statistically significant (adjusted odds ratio 0.17, 95% confidence interval 0.03–1.04). Among patients without respiratory failure at treatment initiation, earlier treatment was associated with lower mortality (adjusted odds ratio 0.17, 95% confidence interval 0.03–0.89). Evidence for other antivirals was limited, and one confirmed treatment-emergent H274Y neuraminidase resistance event was identified. Overall, oseltamivir, particularly when initiated early and before advanced respiratory failure, was associated with improved clinical outcomes, although causal inference remains limited by confounding, heterogeneity, and potentially overlapping study populations.

source_body_en: Human influenza A(H5N1) infection remains a clinically important zoonotic disease, but evidence on antiviral effectiveness is limited by observational designs, heterogeneous treatment timing, and potentially overlapping patient populations. This systematic review synthesized evidence on antiviral regimens, treatment timing, clinical and virological outcomes, and antiviral resistance in laboratory-confirmed human A(H5N1) infection. A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and ScienceDirect was conducted from database inception to 1 July 2026. Methodological quality was assessed using the Newcastle–Ottawa Scale and the JBI Case Series Checklist. The clinical and methodological characteristics varied across studies; consequently, the findings were synthesized narratively. Potential population overlap was considered when synthesizing findings across publications to avoid duplicate aggregation of patient data. Of 2,329 records identified, 22 publications were included. Oseltamivir treatment was associated with a lower hazard of death than no documented anti-influenza antiviral treatment (adjusted hazard ratio 0.51, 95% confidence interval 0.34–0.77). Treatment within 2 days showed lower odds of death, although the overall estimate was not statistically significant (adjusted odds ratio 0.17, 95% confidence interval 0.03–1.04). Among patients without respiratory failure at treatment initiation, earlier treatment was associated with lower mortality (adjusted odds ratio 0.17, 95% confidence interval 0.03–0.89). Evidence for other antivirals was limited, and one confirmed treatment-emergent H274Y neuraminidase resistance event was identified. Overall, oseltamivir, particularly when initiated early and before advanced respiratory failure, was associated with improved clinical outcomes, although causal inference remains limited by confounding, heterogeneity, and potentially overlapping study populations.

title: Rare recovery of reassortants between contemporary clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 viruses and human influenza A viruses in vitro.
abstract: Influenza A virus (IAV) pandemics can arise when animal-derived and human-adapted IAVs exchange genome segments; however, whether contemporary clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 viruses can generate viable reassortants with human IAVs is unclear. Here, we tested the reassortment potential of two clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 viruses with human-adapted H1N1 and H3N2 IAVs using a biosafe reassortment system. Across multiple coinfection conditions, we genotyped 2,698 plaque-purified viral clones and recovered 20 reassortants (0.74%). Polymerase assays identified human IAV subunits, particularly H1N1 PA or H3N2 PB2, that increased H5N1 polymerase activity. Thus, contemporary clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 viruses can reassort with human IAVs, but factors beyond polymerase compatibility may limit their recovery.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Overlapping Miller Fisher Syndrome and Pharyngeal–Cervical–Brachial Variant of Guillain–Barré Syndrome Following Seasonal Influenza Vaccination: A Case Report
abstract: Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) covers a broad spectrum of immune-mediated nerve disorders, including regional subtypes such as Miller Fisher syndrome (MFS) and the pharyngeal-cervical-brachial (PCB) variant.Overlapping features of these variants are recognized but remain uncommon.While it is established that flu vaccination carries a small increased GBS risk, post-vaccination MFS is rare, with overlap presentations being even less frequently reported.A 28-year-old man with no prior medical issues presented with neurological symptoms six days after receiving a seasonal influenza vaccine.His initial presentation included acute bulbar impairment with dysarthria and dysphagia, marked neck weakness causing head drop, binocular diplopia, and distal paresthesia.Examination revealed bilateral ptosis, facial diplegia, left abducens nerve palsy, hypoglossal weakness, limb and gait ataxia, and generalized areflexia.Limb power remained fully preserved.Brain magnetic resonance imaging showed no acute abnormalities.Cerebrospinal fluid analysis demonstrated albuminocytologic dissociation (protein 0.98 g/L).Nerve conduction studies and electromyography identified severe acute motor denervation involving the cranial, cervical, and proximal upper limb muscles, with preserved sensory responses.These findings supported the diagnosis of overlapping MFS and the PCB variant of GBS.Treatment consisted of intravenous immunoglobulin (2 g/kg administered over five days) together with nasogastric feeding because of severe bulbar dysfunction.He made a gradual but significant recovery, with only mild residual imbalance and lagophthalmos at the two-month follow-up.This case highlights a rare overlap of MFS and PCB variants presenting shortly after influenza vaccination, although causality cannot be established.This case highlights the need to think of GBS spectrum disorders in patients who have acute bulbar and oculomotor problems, even with preserved limb strength.Early diagnosis is paramount, as it allows for vigilant monitoring and proactive management of life-threatening sequelae, including respiratory insufficiency and aspiration pneumonia.

title_original: Overlapping Miller Fisher Syndrome and Pharyngeal–Cervical–Brachial Variant of Guillain–Barré Syndrome Following Seasonal Influenza Vaccination: A Case Report

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to report a rare case of overlapping Miller Fisher Syndrome (MFS) and pharyngeal–cervical–brachial (PCB) variant of Guillain–Barré Syndrome (GBS) following seasonal influenza vaccination, highlighting the need to consider GBS spectrum disorders in patients with acute bulbar and oculomotor issues.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A case report was conducted on a 28-year-old man with no prior medical issues who presented with neurological symptoms six days after receiving a seasonal influenza vaccine. The case involved acute bulbar impairment, marked neck weakness, and other neurological manifestations.
analysis.methods: The patient underwent brain magnetic resonance imaging, cerebrospinal fluid analysis, nerve conduction studies, and electromyography to assess the neurological condition. Treatment included intravenous immunoglobulin and nasogastric feeding due to severe bulbar dysfunction.
analysis.main_results: The findings revealed severe acute motor denervation involving cranial, cervical, and proximal upper limb muscles, with preserved sensory responses. These results supported the diagnosis of overlapping MFS and PCB variant of GBS. The patient showed a gradual but significant recovery with mild residual imbalance and lagophthalmos at two-month follow-up.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as a rare presentation of overlapping MFS and PCB variant of GBS following influenza vaccination. They emphasized the importance of early diagnosis to manage life-threatening sequelae, even in the absence of limb weakness.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The case underscores the necessity of considering GBS spectrum disorders in patients presenting with acute bulbar and oculomotor symptoms post-vaccination, which can inform clinical vigilance and management strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: As a case report, the study lacks the statistical power to establish causality, and the findings are limited to a single patient. The evidence is of moderate strength due to the rarity of the condition and the absence of a control group.

analysis.summary_en: This case report describes a rare occurrence of overlapping Miller Fisher Syndrome (MFS) and pharyngeal–cervical–brachial (PCB) variant of Guillain–Barré Syndrome (GBS) following seasonal influenza vaccination. A 28-year-old man presented with acute bulbar impairment, neck weakness, and other neurological symptoms six days post-vaccination. Diagnostic tests confirmed the GBS spectrum disorder, and treatment with intravenous immunoglobulin and nasogastric feeding led to significant recovery. The case highlights the importance of considering GBS variants in patients with bulbar and oculomotor issues, even with preserved limb strength, and emphasizes the need for early diagnosis to prevent life-threatening complications. However, the study's limitations include its single-case design, which restricts the ability to establish causality. The evidence is of moderate strength due to the rarity of the condition and the lack of comparative data.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在报告一例罕见的在接种季节性流感 疫苗接种后出现Miller Fisher综合征(MFS)与咽颈臂(PCB)型吉兰-巴雷综合征(GBS)重叠的病例,强调在出现急性球麻痹和动眼神经症状的患者中应考虑GBS谱系疾病。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 对一名28岁无既往病史的男性进行病例报告,该患者在接种季节性流感 疫苗后六天出现神经系统症状。该病例涉及急性球麻痹、显著颈部无力及其他神经系统表现。
elements_zh.methods: 患者接受了脑磁共振成像、脑脊液分析、神经传导研究和肌电图检查以评估神经系统状况。治疗包括静脉注射免疫球蛋白和鼻饲喂养,以应对严重的球麻痹功能障碍。
elements_zh.main_results: 研究结果表明,出现了严重的急性运动神经元变性,涉及颅神经、颈神经和上肢近端肌肉,但感觉反应保持正常。这些结果支持了重叠MFS与GBS咽颈臂变种的诊断。患者在两个月随访时显示出逐渐但显著的恢复,伴有轻微的平衡障碍和眼睑闭合不全。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为一种罕见的在流感疫苗接种后出现的重叠MFS与GBS咽颈臂变种的表现。他们强调即使在没有肢体无力的情况下,早期诊断对于管理危及生命的后遗症也至关重要。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该病例突显了在流感疫苗接种后出现急性球麻痹和动眼神经症状的患者中考虑GBS谱系疾病的重要性,这可以为临床警觉性和管理策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 作为一项病例报告,该研究缺乏统计效力以确立因果关系,且结果仅限于一名患者。由于该疾病的罕见性以及缺乏对照组,证据强度中等。

abstract_zh: 吉兰-巴利综合征 (GBS) 涵盖广泛的免疫介导的神经疾病,包括米勒·费希尔综合征 (MFS) 和咽颈臂 (PCB) 变异等区域亚型。这些变异的重叠特征已被识别,但仍然不常见。虽然已确定流感 疫苗接种 会略微增加 GBS 风险,但 疫苗接种 后 MFS 很少见,重叠表现甚至更少一名既往没有任何医疗问题的 28 岁男性在接受 季节性流感 疫苗 六天后出现神经系统症状。他的初始症状包括急性延髓损伤伴构音困难和吞咽困难、明显的颈部无力导致头下垂、双眼复视和远端感觉异常。检查显示双侧上睑下垂、面部双瘫、左外展神经麻痹、舌下肌无力、肢体和步态共济失调和全身反射消失。肢体力量仍然完全保留。脑磁共振成像未显示急性异常。脑脊液分析显示白蛋白细胞解离(蛋白质 0.98 g/L)。神经传导研究和肌电图确定了涉及颅骨、颈椎和近端上肢肌肉的严重急性运动去神经支配,并保留了感觉反应。这些发现支持重叠 MFS 的 诊断 和 PCB 变体GBS.治疗 由于严重的延髓功能障碍,需要静脉注射免疫球蛋白(2 g/kg,持续五天)并鼻饲。他逐渐但显着地康复,在两个月的随访中仅出现轻微的残余失衡和兔眼症。该病例强调了流感 疫苗接种 后不久出现的 MFS 和 PCB 变异的罕见重叠,尽管无法确定因果关系。该病例强调需要考虑 GBS 谱系疾病患有急性延髓和动眼神经问题的患者,即使肢体力量得以保留。早期 诊断 至关重要,因为它可以对危及生命的后遗症进行警惕监测和主动管理,包括呼吸功能不全和吸入性肺炎。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在报告一例罕见的在接种季节性流感 疫苗接种后出现Miller Fisher综合征(MFS)与咽颈臂(PCB)型吉兰-巴雷综合征(GBS)重叠的病例,强调在出现急性球麻痹和动眼神经症状的患者中应考虑GBS谱系疾病。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 对一名28岁无既往病史的男性进行病例报告,该患者在接种季节性流感 疫苗后六天出现神经系统症状。该病例涉及急性球麻痹、显著颈部无力及其他神经系统表现。
analysis_zh.methods: 患者接受了脑磁共振成像、脑脊液分析、神经传导研究和肌电图检查以评估神经系统状况。治疗包括静脉注射免疫球蛋白和鼻饲喂养,以应对严重的球麻痹功能障碍。
analysis_zh.main_results: 研究结果表明,出现了严重的急性运动神经元变性,涉及颅神经、颈神经和上肢近端肌肉,但感觉反应保持正常。这些结果支持了重叠MFS与GBS咽颈臂变种的诊断。患者在两个月随访时显示出逐渐但显著的恢复,伴有轻微的平衡障碍和眼睑闭合不全。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为一种罕见的在流感疫苗接种后出现的重叠MFS与GBS咽颈臂变种的表现。他们强调即使在没有肢体无力的情况下,早期诊断对于管理危及生命的后遗症也至关重要。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该病例突显了在流感疫苗接种后出现急性球麻痹和动眼神经症状的患者中考虑GBS谱系疾病的重要性,这可以为临床警觉性和管理策略提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 作为一项病例报告,该研究缺乏统计效力以确立因果关系,且结果仅限于一名患者。由于该疾病的罕见性以及缺乏对照组,证据强度中等。

title: Cul4b sustains cell cycle in germinal center B cells and enables protective humoral immunity against influenza A virus.
abstract: Influenza A viruses (IAVs) are a major public health burden, infecting millions of people worldwide. Seasonal vaccines mitigate disease, in part, by triggering the production of IAV-specific antibodies by B cells. Viral evasion and limited vaccine-induced immunity pose barriers to vaccine effectiveness, warranting further investigation of factors influencing protective immune responses. The generation of affinity-matured antibodies is critical for antiviral immunity. This relies on germinal center (GC) B cells, which undergo multiple rounds of somatic hypermutation, proliferation, and selection. Cullin-4b (Cul4b) acts as the backbone for the Cullin Ring Ligase 4 (CRL4), an E3 ubiquitin ligase complex that ubiquitylates proteins for degradation by the proteosome. CRL4 is critical for regulation of DNA damage responses and cell cycle maintenance, essential for B cells to mount a robust humoral response. Here we investigate the role of Cul4b in B cell responses to IAV using mice lacking Cul4b in B cells. We found that Cul4b promoted viral clearance and anti-IAV antibody titers post-infection and immunization, and Cul4b was required for optimal vaccine-mediated protection against infectious challenge. Additionally, we found that Cul4b supports GC B cell populations and promotes their cell cycle maintenance in vivo. We conclude that B cell intrinsic Cul4b is essential for optimal GC and antibody responses after acute IAV exposure. Further investigation of CRL4 in B cells is warranted to elucidate its potential as a therapeutic target to improve vaccine efficacy.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the role of Cul4b in B cell responses to influenza A virus (IAV) using mice lacking Cul4b in B cells. It highlights that Cul4b is essential for optimal germinal center (GC) and antibody responses after acute IAV exposure, promoting viral clearance and anti-IAV antibody titers post-infection and immunization. The findings suggest that Cul4b supports GC B cell populations and their cell cycle maintenance in vivo, which may have implications for improving vaccine efficacy against IAV. The study provides novel insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying B cell function in antiviral immunity, but it does not report specific limitations. The evidence strength is high due to the direct experimental findings.

title_zh: Cul4b维持生发中心B细胞的细胞周期并促进对甲型流感病毒的保护性体液免疫。
source_body_en: Influenza A viruses (IAVs) are a major public health burden, infecting millions of people worldwide. Seasonal vaccines mitigate disease, in part, by triggering the production of IAV-specific antibodies by B cells. Viral evasion and limited vaccine-induced immunity pose barriers to vaccine effectiveness, warranting further investigation of factors influencing protective immune responses. The generation of affinity-matured antibodies is critical for antiviral immunity. This relies on germinal center (GC) B cells, which undergo multiple rounds of somatic hypermutation, proliferation, and selection. Cullin-4b (Cul4b) acts as the backbone for the Cullin Ring Ligase 4 (CRL4), an E3 ubiquitin ligase complex that ubiquitylates proteins for degradation by the proteosome. CRL4 is critical for regulation of DNA damage responses and cell cycle maintenance, essential for B cells to mount a robust humoral response. Here we investigate the role of Cul4b in B cell responses to IAV using mice lacking Cul4b in B cells. We found that Cul4b promoted viral clearance and anti-IAV antibody titers post-infection and immunization, and Cul4b was required for optimal vaccine-mediated protection against infectious challenge. Additionally, we found that Cul4b supports GC B cell populations and promotes their cell cycle maintenance in vivo. We conclude that B cell intrinsic Cul4b is essential for optimal GC and antibody responses after acute IAV exposure. Further investigation of CRL4 in B cells is warranted to elucidate its potential as a therapeutic target to improve vaccine efficacy.
abstract_zh: 甲型流感病毒(IAVs)是重大的公共卫生负担,每年感染全球数百万人。季节性流感疫苗通过促使B细胞产生针对IAV的特异性抗体来部分减轻疾病。病毒逃逸和有限的疫苗诱导的免疫反应限制了疫苗的有效性,因此需要进一步研究影响保护性免疫反应的因素。亲和力成熟的抗体对于疫苗诱导的免疫反应至关重要。这依赖于生发中心(GC)B细胞,其经历多轮体细胞超突变、增殖和选择。Cullin-4b(Cul4b)作为Cullin Ring Ligase 4(CRL4)复合体的骨架,该复合体是一种E3泛素连接酶,通过泛素化蛋白质促进其被蛋白酶体降解。CRL4对于调控DNA损伤反应和细胞周期维持至关重要,这是B细胞产生强效体液免疫反应所必需的。在这里,我们利用缺乏B细胞中Cul4b的小鼠,研究Cul4b在B细胞对IAV反应中的作用。我们发现,Cul4b促进了感染和免疫接种后病毒的清除和抗IAV抗体滴度的升高,并且Cul4b对于通过疫苗诱导的保护性免疫反应是必需的。此外,我们还发现Cul4b支持生发中心B细胞群体的维持,并促进其在体内的细胞周期维持。我们得出结论,B细胞内源性的Cul4b对于急性IAV暴露后生发中心和抗体反应的优化至关重要。进一步研究B细胞中的CRL4对于阐明其作为改善疫苗效果的潜在治疗靶点具有重要意义。

title: Self-amplifying RNA vaccines encoding chimeric and mosaic hemagglutinins confer immunity against phylogenetically diverse influenza A viruses.
abstract: Seasonal influenza vaccines require annual reformulation due to antigenic drift and provide suboptimal protection. Here, we evaluate self-amplifying mRNA (samRNA) vaccines encoding chimeric (cHA) and mosaic (mHA) hemagglutinins representing influenza A virus HA phylogenetic groups 1 and 2. Following prime-boost immunization, group 1 cHA vaccines (cH8/1-cH5/1) elicit broad cross-reactive antibodies and confer complete protection against diverse H1N1 strains covering decades of antigenic drift. Group 2 vaccines (cH4/3-cH15/3 and mH10/3-mH14/3) provide comparable breadth against multiple H3N2 strains and heterosubtypic H7N9 challenge, with cHA samRNA showing superior cross-group protection. Protection is associated with Fc-mediated effector functions and CD4 + T cell responses, with minimal hemagglutination inhibition and neutralizing titers. Passive serum transfer confirms antibody-mediated protection independent of cellular immunity. Protective immunity is maintained at doses as low as 0.4 μg, demonstrating the dose-sparing advantage of the samRNA platform. These results support samRNA-delivered cHA and mHA antigens as promising candidates for broadly protective influenza vaccines.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates self-amplifying RNA vaccines encoding chimeric and mosaic hemagglutinins against seasonal influenza viruses. The research addresses the need for vaccines that can provide broader protection against antigenic drift. The study demonstrates that group 1 cHA vaccines confer complete protection against diverse H1N1 strains, while group 2 vaccines offer comparable breadth against H3N2 strains and H7N9 challenge. The findings suggest that these vaccines may offer a promising approach for broadly protective influenza vaccines. The results highlight the role of Fc-mediated effector functions and CD4+ T cell responses in protection, with minimal reliance on hemagglutination inhibition and neutralizing titers. The study also shows that protective immunity can be achieved at low doses, indicating a dose-sparing advantage. However, the evidence is limited to the specific vaccine formulations tested and does not address broader implications or limitations in real-world application.

abstract_zh: 季节性流感 疫苗由于抗原漂移需要每年重新配制,且提供不充分的保护。在此,我们评估了自我扩增型mRNA(samRNA)疫苗,其编码代表甲型流感病毒HA系统发育群1和2的嵌合(cHA)和镶嵌(mHA)血凝素。在接种加强针后,群组1的cHA 疫苗(cH8/1-cH5/1)可引发广泛的交叉反应性抗体,并对覆盖数十年抗原漂移的多种H1N1毒株提供完全保护。群组2的疫苗(cH4/3-cH15/3和mH10/3-mH14/3)对多种H3N2毒株和异亚型H7N9挑战提供相当的广度保护,其中cHA samRNA表现出更优的跨群组保护能力。保护作用与Fc介导的效应功能和CD4 + T细胞反应相关,且血凝抑制和中和抗体滴度较低。被动血清转移实验确认了抗体介导的保护作用,且不依赖于细胞免疫。保护性免疫可在低至0.4 μg剂量下维持,这展示了samRNA平台的剂量节省优势。这些结果支持通过samRNA递送的cHA和mHA抗原作为广泛保护性流感疫苗的有前景候选物。

title: Validation of chemical inactivation methods for Select Agent compliance using HPAIV and low-pathogenicity influenza A virus in tissues and cultured cells
abstract: The US Federal Select Agent program requires that inactivation procedures be validated before treated materials can be removed from biocontainment for downstream use. Although H5 avian influenza viruses are subject to temporary exemption from the Select Agent regulatory requirements, validated inactivation workflows remain critical for safe downstream handling of HPAIV-containing materials. Common treatments, including TRIzol, TRIzol LS, formalin, and ice-cold methanol, are frequently used to facilitate virus inactivation and downstream processing. However, facility-specific inactivation validation is required for Select Agent workflows and for safe handling of HPAIV-containing materials. In this study, HPAIV (H5N1)-infected samples were used to validate inactivation of material generated in cell culture, and low-pathogenicity (H1N1)-infected lung homogenates were used to validate inactivation of animal-derived tissues. Following inactivation, column-based buffer exchange was used to remove cytotoxic inactivants before viability testing. This step did not significantly reduce recovery of infectious virus, supporting the sensitivity of this approach. In inactivation tests, residual infectious virus was assessed by plaque assay and serial blind passages. No infectious virus was detected following any of the tested conditions. These data validate several procedures for inactivating influenza A virus-containing cell cultures, fluids, and tissue samples and provide a framework for facility-specific validation of similar workflows.

analysis.summary_en: This study validates chemical inactivation methods for Select Agent compliance using HPAIV (H5N1) and low-pathogenicity influenza A (H1N1) viruses in cell culture and animal-derived tissues. The methods involved plaque assay, serial blind passages, and column-based buffer exchange to assess virus inactivation. No infectious virus was detected after inactivation, supporting the effectiveness of the procedures. The results provide a framework for facility-specific validation of similar workflows, which has implications for safe handling of influenza A virus-containing materials. The study's general evidence suggests the methods are sensitive and effective, though no specific limitations are reported, resulting in a moderate confidence assessment.

title: Influenza Infection, Newly Diagnosed Atrial Fibrillation, and One-Year Mortality in Hospitalized Adults: A Retrospective Cohort Study
abstract: Background/Objectives: Whether influenza increases the risk of newly diagnosed atrial fibrillation (NDAF) beyond the effect of acute illness is uncertain. We examined whether viral etiology and prior influenza vaccination (exposures) were associated with NDAF within one year (primary outcome), and whether NDAF was associated with one-year all-cause mortality (secondary outcome), in hospitalized adults. Methods: This retrospective cohort study included 21,653 adults hospitalized in Clalit Health Services facilities (2012–2020) who underwent respiratory-virus PCR testing: influenza A (n = 2829), influenza B (n = 992), other respiratory viruses (n = 561), and PCR-negative concurrent controls (n = 17,271). NDAF within 365 days was analyzed with cause-specific Cox and Fine–Gray models, including time windows; mortality with time-dependent Cox models; and vaccination with propensity score matching. Results: NDAF was recorded in 1228 patients (5.7%), 56% of them on the day of admission. Compared with PCR-negative patients, no viral etiology was associated with a higher hazard of NDAF (influenza A: HR 0.87, 95% CI 0.73–1.04; influenza B: HR 0.73, 95% CI 0.53–1.00), including within 30 days and after excluding day-0 events. NDAF was associated with higher one-year mortality (HR 1.68, 95% CI 1.52–1.87), especially when recorded after discharge (HR 3.04). Influenza vaccination was not associated with NDAF (HR 0.97, 95% CI 0.85–1.10). Conclusions: Among hospitalized adults tested for respiratory viruses, neither influenza nor prior vaccination was associated with NDAF compared with PCR-negative inpatients, who were not necessarily of similar acute illness severity. NDAF marked a higher hazard of one-year mortality.

title: Seasonal H1N1 influenza A virus preferentially infects a pre-existing ciliogenesis-primed secretory cell state
abstract: Influenza A viruses (IAV) infect secretory and ciliated cells of the human airway epithelium , but whether all cells within one cell type are equally susceptible to infection remains unresolved. Here, single-cell RNA sequencing analysis of primary human bronchial epithelial cultures from three donors identified preferential infection of a transcriptionally distinct subpopulation of secretory cells by seasonal H1N1 IAV A/Hawaii/70/2019 . Genes upregulated in this subpopulation showed enrichment for cilium-related gene ontology terms. In an ex post facto approach, this enrichment persisted after excluding genes differentially expressed between infected and mock-treated samples, including those identified in secretory cell-specific comparisons. Single-cell analysis further revealed no significant increase in ciliogenesis scores in infected secretory cells compared to mock infected cells at 6 hours post-infection , arguing against infection-induced activation of the canonical ciliogenesis programme during the initial viral replication cycle . Collectively, these results support preferential infection of ciliogenesis-primed secretory cells and refine IAV tropism beyond cell type to encompass epithelial differentiation state.

analysis.methods: Single-cell RNA sequencing was used to analyze primary human bronchial epithelial cultures from three donors, identifying a transcriptionally distinct subpopulation of secretory cells preferentially infected by seasonal H1N1 IAV A/Hawaii/70/2019.

analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These results support preferential infection of ciliogenesis-primed secretory cells and refine IAV tropism beyond cell type to encompass epithelial differentiation state.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings refine our understanding of IAV tropism and suggest that epithelial differentiation state may influence susceptibility to seasonal influenza viruses.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its ex post facto approach and small sample size, but the evidence is strong given the use of single-cell RNA sequencing and the consistency of results across three donors.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the susceptibility of secretory cells to seasonal H1N1 influenza A virus infection. Using single-cell RNA sequencing on primary human bronchial epithelial cultures from three donors, the research identifies a transcriptionally distinct subpopulation of secretory cells that are preferentially infected by the virus. The results show that genes in this subpopulation are enriched for cilium-related functions, suggesting that ciliogenesis-primed secretory cells may be more susceptible to infection. The study contributes to understanding IAV tropism by highlighting the role of epithelial differentiation state in viral susceptibility. However, the ex post facto design and small sample size limit the confidence in the findings, though the evidence is considered strong due to the robust methodology and consistent results across donors.

abstract_zh: 流感病毒A(IAV)感染人类气道上皮的分泌细胞和纤毛细胞,但是否所有同一细胞类型的细胞对感染的易感性都相同仍未明确。在这里,对来自三位供体的原代人类支气管上皮培养物进行单细胞RNA测序分析,发现季节性H1N1 IAV A/Hawaii/70/2019优先感染一个转录特征不同的分泌细胞亚群。该亚群中上调的基因在纤毛相关基因本体(GO)术语中表现出富集。采用事后分析方法,这种富集在排除感染与假处理样本之间差异表达的基因后仍然存在,包括在分泌细胞特异性比较中识别出的基因。单细胞分析进一步显示,在感染后6小时,感染的分泌细胞与假感染细胞相比,纤毛生成评分没有显著增加,这反驳了在病毒初始复制周期中感染诱导经典纤毛生成程序激活的观点。总体而言,这些结果支持已预先启动纤毛生成的分泌细胞优先感染,并将IAV的嗜性从细胞类型扩展到上皮分化状态。

title: Triterpenoid saponins from the aerial parts of Phytolacca americana and their anti-influenza A virus activity
abstract: Abstract Phytolacca americana L. (Phytolaccaceae), a perennial species native to North America, is rich in oleanane-type triterpenoid saponins. In this study, ultra-performance liquid chromatography coupled with quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry (UPLC–QTOF–MS) profiling of the aerial-part extract revealed characteristic fragment ions of phytolaccagenin- and phytolaccagenic acid-type saponins with diverse glycosylation. MS-guided annotation enabled targeted isolation and structural elucidation of two previously undescribed compounds, one oleanane-type triterpenoid saponin (1) and one neolignan (3). Additionally, compound 2, which had been reported only based on mass spectrometric data, was isolated, and its structure was fully elucidated for the first time, together with those of 10 known oleanane-type triterpenoid saponins (4–13). Their structures were elucidated by comprehensive one-dimensional and two-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopic analyses combined with UPLC–QTOF–MS data. americana extracts have been reported to inhibit influenza A virus infection in previous studies, the bioactive constituents responsible for this antiviral activity have not been identified. The crude extract and isolated saponins were evaluated using complementary in vitro assays. In H1N1-infected A549 cells, compound 11 (3-O-trisaccharide phytolaccagenic acid) reduced viral NS1 RNA levels at 6 and 24 hpi as determined by RT–qPCR. Antiviral activity was further confirmed by plaque reduction and immunoblot analyses, with a plaque-assay IC50 of 57.98 ± 0.26 μM.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the bioactive constituents of Phytolacca americana extracts responsible for their anti-influenza A virus activity. The research focuses on identifying specific compounds that may contribute to the observed antiviral effects. Using in vitro assays on H1N1-infected A549 cells, the study demonstrates that compound 11, a 3-O-trisaccharide phytolaccagenic acid, reduces viral NS1 RNA levels at 6 and 24 hpi. The findings suggest that certain saponins from this plant may have therapeutic potential against seasonal influenza. However, the study is limited to in vitro experiments and a single strain, which may restrict the generalisability of the results. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the lack of in vivo data and broader strain testing.

abstract_zh: 摘要 美洲商陆(Phytolacca americana L.,Phytolaccaceae科)是一种原产于北美的多年生植物,富含齐墩果烷型三萜皂苷。本研究通过超高效液相色谱-四极杆时间飞行质谱(UPLC–QTOF–MS)分析美洲商陆地上部分提取物,揭示了具有多样糖基化的拟商陆皂苷(phytolaccagenin-和phytolaccagenic acid型)的特征碎片离子。通过质谱引导的注释,实现了对两种此前未被描述的化合物的靶向分离和结构鉴定,其中一种是齐墩果烷型三萜皂苷(1),另一种是新木脂素(3)。此外,化合物2(此前仅基于质谱数据报道)被分离,并首次对其结构进行了完整阐明,同时阐明了10种已知齐墩果烷型三萜皂苷(4–13)的结构。这些结构通过综合的一维和二维核磁共振光谱分析结合UPLC–QTOF–MS数据得以阐明。此前有报道称美洲商陆提取物可抑制甲型流感病毒感染,但其生物活性成分尚未被鉴定。本研究使用互补的体外实验评估了粗提物和分离的皂苷。在H1N1感染的A549细胞中,化合物11(3-O-三糖拟商陆酸)通过RT–qPCR检测,在感染后6小时和24小时降低了病毒NS1 RNA水平。该抗病毒活性进一步通过斑块减少和免疫印迹分析得到证实,其中斑块实验的IC50为57.98 ± 0.26 μM。

title: Weekly dynamics, subtype replacement and regional heterogeneity of influenza activity in China, 2024-2026: A national sentinel surveillance analysis.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: National influenza surveillance in China is reported weekly, but recent post-pandemic patterns integrating regional timing, subtype/lineage replacement and outbreak activity have not been quantitatively characterized in a continuous national series. We aimed to reconstruct and quantify weekly influenza dynamics in China from 2024/W01 to 2026/W21. METHODS: We performed a retrospective secondary time-series analysis of 125 publicly available, aggregate weekly reports from the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention and Chinese National Influenza Center. Values were reconciled against official reports when working datasets differed or quality-control checks identified inconsistencies. Positivity was recalculated from positive and tested specimens. Regional differences were evaluated across paired weeks using heteroskedasticity- and autocorrelation-consistent Newey-West standard errors and exploratory lead-lag relationships were assessed using cross-correlation of first-differenced weekly series. RESULTS: Nationally, 1,796,636 influenza-like illness specimens were tested and 253,219 were influenza-positive (weighted positivity, 14.1%); national positivity peaked in 2025/W49 at 49.8%. Overall weighted positivity was 14.6% in Southern China and 13.3% in Northern China. Across 125 paired weeks, Southern China had a mean positivity 4.41 percentage points higher than Northern China (95% CI, 2.23-6.59; P < 0.001) and a mean ILI percentage 0.77 points higher (95% CI, 0.48-1.05; P < 0.001). First-difference positivity changes were most strongly correlated when Northern China led Southern China by one week (r = 0.781). Among 253,104 explicitly reported subtype/lineage detections, A(H3N2) was largest (45.6%), followed by A(H1N1)pdm09 (33.8%) and B(Victoria) (20.6%). Predominance followed A(H3N2) in 2024/W01, B(Victoria), A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3N2) and B(Victoria) again in early 2026. Reported outbreaks peaked in 2025/W48 at 1,541, during A(H3N2) predominance. CONCLUSIONS: Recent influenza activity in China was multi-wave and regionally heterogeneous, with measurable north-south temporal differences, sequential subtype replacement and a large A(H3N2)-associated outbreak surge. The analysis also demonstrates the importance of explicit source-level quality control when reusing aggregated public surveillance reports.

CONCLUSIONS: Recent influenza activity in China was multi-wave and regionally heterogeneous, with measurable north-south temporal differences, sequential subtype replacement and a large A(H3N2)-associated outbreak surge. title: Mosaic Hemagglutinin-Based Influenza B mRNA-LNP Vaccine Induces Strong Humoral Immune Response in Non-Human Primates.
abstract: Developing broadly protective influenza vaccines remains a major challenge for global public health. Influenza B viruses cause about one-third of all annual influenza virus infections and current vaccines only show moderate effectiveness against matched virus strains, therefore, development of more effective and broadly protective vaccines against them is important. Chimeric and mosaic hemagglutinin (cHA and mHA) immunogens are under investigation as broadly protective influenza B vaccine candidates. The lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-encapsulated nucleoside-modified mRNA technology has recently revolutionized vaccination and gained widespread interest due to its successful use in the coronavirus disease 2019 pandemic. Here, we evaluated influenza B cHA and mHA mRNA-LNP vaccines in non-human primates and compared their immunogenicity to a quadrivalent seasonal influenza virus vaccine. mHA mRNA-LNPs induced high binding antibody titers against antigenically distant influenza B virus strains, with significant hemagglutination inhibition and antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity activity and provided protection in mice in a serum transfer challenge experiment. This approach shows great promise for developing broadly protective influenza B vaccines.
journal: Molecular therapy : the journal of the American Society of Gene Therapy

title: Effectiveness of the 2025-2026 trivalent influenza vaccine against laboratory-confirmed influenza among older adults in Eastern China: A test-negative case-control study.
abstract: Evidence on the real-world effectiveness of seasonal influenza vaccination among older adults in China remains limited and varies by season and circulating virus. We used a test-negative case-control design to estimate the effectiveness of the 2025-2026 trivalent influenza vaccine against medically attended, laboratory-confirmed influenza among adults aged ≥60 years attending two sentinel hospitals in Shengzhou, Zhejiang Province. Participants vaccinated ≥14 days before symptom onset were considered vaccinated; those vaccinated 0-13 days before onset were excluded from the primary analysis. Vaccine effectiveness (VE) was calculated as (1 - adjusted odds ratio) × 100% using multivariable logistic regression. Among 532 participants in the primary analysis, 156 were influenza-positive cases and 376 were test-negative controls. Effective current-season vaccination was recorded in 32.7% of cases and 48.4% of controls. Adjusted VE against any influenza was 46% (95% confidence interval [CI], 18-64). Type-specific VE was 42% (95% CI, 8-63) against influenza A and 60% (95% CI, 14-81) against influenza B. Subtype-specific estimates were less precise, and interaction analyses did not identify differences by age group or chronic-disease status. The overall estimate remained stable across diagnostic restrictions and alternative model specifications. The 2025-2026 trivalent influenza vaccine was associated with moderate protection against medically attended influenza in older adults under routine program conditions, supporting continued seasonal vaccination and multi-season surveillance.

title: Pediatric Influenza Vaccine Effectiveness Against Emergency Visits and Hospitalization in Canada: 2024-2025 and 2025-2026 seasons
abstract: ABSTRACT Importance Influenza causes substantial morbidity in children, yet Canadian data on influenza vaccine effectiveness (VE) in preventing emergency department (ED) visits and hospitalizations are limited. Objective To estimate VE against influenza-associated ED visits and hospitalizations among children during the 2024-2025 and 2025-2026 seasons. Design Test-negative case-control design. Setting Fourteen Canadian pediatric tertiary-care hospitals participating in the Surveillance Program for the Rapid IdeNtification and TracKing of Infectious Diseases in kidS (SPRINT-KIDS) network. Participants Symptomatic children aged 6 months to <18 years tested for influenza from October 27, 2024, to June 7, 2025, and from November 2, 2025, to June 13, 2026. Exposure At least one dose of current-season influenza vaccine. Main Outcomes and Measures VE against laboratory-confirmed influenza A or B associated with an ED visit or hospitalization. VE was estimated using multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, epidemiologic week, site, and high-risk comorbidity. Results The 2024-2025 season included 17,316 encounters (median [IQR] age=41.0 [18.5–82.3] months; 54.0% male), with 4,760 influenza-positive cases (8.9% vaccinated) and 12,556 influenza-negative controls (15.9% vaccinated). The 2025-2026 season included 13,417 encounters (median [IQR] age=33.5 [16.7–74.8] months; 54.1% male), with 4,798 cases (7.6% vaccinated) and 8,619 controls (18.1% vaccinated). VE against any influenza was 47% (95%CI, 40–53%) and 53% (95%CI, 46–59%) in 2024-2025 and 2025-2026, respectively. VE against ED visits was 53% (95%CI, 45–59%) and 57% (95%CI, 49–63%), and VE against hospitalization was 33% (95%CI, 16–47%) and 48% (95%CI, 33–59%) in 2024-2025 and 2025-2026, respectively. VE was lower against influenza A as compared to B in both seasons: 31% (95%CI, 22–39%) vs. 75% (95%CI, 64– 82%) (p<0.001) in 2024-2025; and 42% (95%CI, 32–50%) vs. 64% (95%CI, 55–72%) (p=0.001) in 2025-2026. VE was lower in children aged 10 to <18 years than in those <10 years, particularly among children with comorbidities. Protection against influenza A lasted up to 90 days, whereas it persisted beyond 120 days for influenza B. Conclusions and Relevance Influenza vaccines were moderately effective against pediatric ED visits and hospitalizations in both seasons. Routine vaccination should continue to be recommended to prevent hospital-attended influenza. Key Points Question How effective were influenza vaccines against influenza-associated emergency department visits and hospitalizations among Canadian children during the 2024-2025 and 2025-2026 seasons? Findings In this test-negative case-control study of 30,733 encounters at 14 pediatric hospitals, vaccine effectiveness against any influenza was 47% in 2024-2025 and 53% in 2025-2026, despite antigenically drifted A(H3N2) subclade K predominance. Effectiveness was lower against influenza A than B and among adolescents. Meaning These findings support continued annual influenza vaccination of children, even when substantial antigenic mismatch is anticipated.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the effectiveness of influenza vaccines against emergency department (ED) visits and hospitalizations due to influenza in Canadian children during the 2024-2025 and 2025-2026 seasons. Using a test-negative case-control design, the research included 17,316 and 13,417 encounters across 14 pediatric hospitals. Vaccine effectiveness (VE) against any influenza was 47% and 53% in the two seasons, respectively, with higher effectiveness observed against influenza B compared to A. VE against ED visits was 53% and 57%, while against hospitalization it was 33% and 48%. The study highlights the importance of continued vaccination despite antigenic drift, particularly for influenza A. The findings are based on a robust design but do not address limitations explicitly.

title: Deciphering Viral Antigenic Relationships Through Antigenic Cartography: A Narrative Review
abstract: Background: Antigenic cartography is a computational approach that quantitatively visualizes antigenic relationships among viral strains using serological data, including hemagglutination inhibition and virus-neutralization assays. Since its introduction in the early 2000s, it has substantially advanced the study of viral antigenic evolution by transforming complex serological measurements into interpretable antigenic maps, thereby facilitating assessment of antigenic diversity, immune escape, cross-reactivity, and vaccine–virus relationships. Objective: This review examines the historical development, methodological principles, applications, limitations, and emerging directions of antigenic cartography across clinically relevant viruses, with particular emphasis on its relevance to viral surveillance, antigenic drift monitoring and vaccine-strain selection. Methods: The literature was synthesized comparatively across major applications of antigenic cartography, encompassing human seasonal influenza and other viruses, including dengue, lyssaviruses, foot-and-mouth disease virus, Enterovirus A71, norovirus, rotavirus, SARS-CoV-2, and HIV. Particular attention was given to real-world applications, methodological advances, sources of uncertainty, and integration with genomic, structural, evolutionary, and computational approaches. Findings: Influenza remains the most extensively studied viral pathogen, where antigenic cartography has supported recognition of epidemiologically relevant antigenic transitions and informed vaccine decisions. Examples include the emergence of A/Fujian/411/2002-like H3N2 viruses during 2004–2005 and assessment of A/California/07/2009 during 2010–2011. Applications to other viruses demonstrate broader utility for characterizing antigenic landscapes and evaluating cross-protective immunity and vaccine performance. However, map reliability is influenced by serological assay variability, serum-panel composition, measurement noise, incomplete and geographically biased datasets. Limited inter-operability among serological, genomic, and structural datasets further restricts reproducibility and cross-study comparability. Future Directions and Conclusions: The field is transitioning from retrospective visualization toward predictive and mechanistically informed antigenic surveillance. Integration of artificial intelligence, protein language models, evolutionary modelling, structural vaccinology, and real-time genomic–serological surveillance could enable earlier prediction of antigenic drift, identification of emerging vaccine mismatches, and prioritization of candidate vaccine strains. Future platforms should incorporate standardized and automated serological measurements, inter-laboratory calibration, harmonized data standards, geographically representative datasets, experimental validation, and interpretable continuously updated models. Such integration could establish antigenic cartography as a scalable predictive framework for vaccine design and for strengthening preparedness against emerging viral threats.

title: A glycosylation-associated hemagglutinin substitution improves the breadth of an influenza B mRNA vaccine
abstract: Introduction Influenza B virus is an important cause of seasonal influenza, with its contribution varying across regions and seasons. Historically, influenza B viruses have been classified into two major lineages: B/Victoria (BV) and B/Yamagata. No naturally circulating B/Yamagata-lineage viruses have been confirmed after March 2020, making protection against BV the current priority of influenza B vaccination. In our previous study, we demonstrated that the T214A mutation significantly alters the cross-neutralization capacity of this antigen, potentially through altered glycosylation. Notably, the WHO-recommended vaccine strain for the season, B/Austria/1359417/2021 (BV21), lacked the relevant glycosylation position. Methods We used an mRNA platform to compare the cross-subclade protection provided by B/Wyoming/06/2014 (BW06) and BV21 within the B/Victoria lineage. We also introduced the D212N substitution into BV21 as a minimal antigenic modification. Results The D212N substitution restored the glycosylation motif in BV21 and enhanced cross-neutralizing responses against the tested heterologous strains. Mice immunized with a high dose of the D212N-modified vaccine showed 100% survival following challenge with the tested viruses from different subclades. Discussion Our findings provide valuable insights for the development of broadly protective influenza B vaccines.

No naturally circulating B/Yamagata-lineage viruses have been confirmed after March 2020, making protection against BV the current priority of influenza B vaccination. title: Live attenuated YFV-17D vaccine induces robust B and T cell immunity in vaccine-draining lymph nodes
abstract: The yellow fever virus-17D (YFV-17D) vaccine is widely regarded as one of the most effective vaccines in existence, with protection linked to robust elicitation of neutralising antibodies1. The features of the germinal centre (GC) reaction driving this durable and potent antibody responses remain unclear. Here we examined immune dynamics in blood and lymph nodes (LNs) after primary YFV-17D immunisation in humans. Using fine needle biopsy (FNB), we identified robust T and B lymphocyte responses within draining LNs, underpinning maturation of antibodies targeting the viral envelope (E). Early antibody responses were largely IgM, with gradual accumulation of E-specific memory B cells and anti-viral IgG in the subsequent months. Monoclonal antibodies derived from GC B cells had specificity for E, with diversification in the LN capable of driving increases in binding and neutralising potency. While circulating vaccine-specific CD4+ T cells peaked two weeks post-vaccination, clonally related GC and IL-10+ T follicular helper populations progressively accumulated in the LN. Comparison of FNB transcriptional datasets following YFV-17D, SARS-CoV-2 mRNA/LNP, and seasonal influenza vaccination identified a conserved GC program involving similar B and T lymphocyte subpopulations. Collectively, we find that while YFV-17D induces robust GC activity, this trait is shared with other vaccine platforms and the notably durable protection against infection may reflect an incapacity of the virus to escape host immunity.

title: Evaluation of targets for normalization of viral pathogen concentrations in building dust.
abstract: Building dust is potentially an important public health tool for monitoring human pathogens because it contains genetic material from pathogens. However, building dust is heterogeneous and presents technical challenges for environmental pathogen surveillance. To effectively use pathogen measurements in building dust for environmental surveillance, normalization procedures that account for human contribution to dust may be necessary and could help account for variability in occupancy and temporal resolution. Our analysis investigates potential indicators of human emission that could be used to normalize data on concentration of pathogens in dust. Ninety-nine vacuum dust samples were collected from 33 buildings and concentrations were measured for three emission indicators ( i.e. , human cytochrome B gene, Carjivirus communis (previously crAssphage), and pepper mild mottle virus) and two respiratory pathogens ( i.e. SARS-CoV-2 and influenza A virus). All of these were detected in ≥91% of the samples, with the exception of influenza A virus (73%). Most pairings of indicators (nine of 10) showed a weak to moderate positive correlation with one another (Kendall's τ ≤ 0.28). Correlations between occupancy and emission indicators and respiratory pathogens were weak (Kendall's τ p > 0.1). Among all potential markers, MT-CYB was most promising, with detection in 96% of the samples, higher concentration than others, and stronger correlation with other potential measures of occupancy.

title: Influenza Vaccination and Cardiovascular Protection: Current and Emerging Evidence in Primary and Secondary Prevention
abstract: Influenza infection is increasingly recognized as an important cardiovascular risk factor beyond its traditional role as a respiratory illness. Influenza infection may precipitate myocardial infarction, stroke, heart failure exacerbation, and arrhythmias through systemic inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, thrombosis, and plaque destabilization. Growing evidence suggests that influenza vaccination may reduce cardiovascular events and hospitalization in both primary and secondary prevention settings, particularly among older adults and high-risk cardiovascular populations. Contemporary American and European guidelines increasingly recognize influenza vaccination as part of preventive cardiology and secondary cardiovascular prevention. This narrative review summarizes current evidence regarding influenza vaccination in primary and secondary cardiovascular prevention, with emphasis on mechanistic pathways, clinical outcomes, and future preventive strategies.

title: Emerging Technologies and Artificial Intelligence for Avian Influenza: Transmission Dynamics, Interspecies Spread, and Early Warning
abstract: Avian influenza remains a major global threat. It causes recurring outbreaks, economic losses, and public health concerns. Avian influenza virus (AIV) circulates naturally in wild waterfowl. Recent outbreaks have raised concerns about viral evolution and cross-species transmission. Infections in mammals, including dairy cattle and humans, highlight the need for stronger surveillance. This integrative narrative review examines AIV epidemiology, viral evolution, host adaptation, and transmission pathways. It gives particular attention to dust and aerosol exposure. It also considers interactions among wild birds, poultry, and mammals. Structured searches of PubMed and Scopus covered the literature from January 2015 to 12 December 2025. Selected 2026 publications provided additional context. The review synthesizes scientific studies, outbreak investigations, and epidemiological reports. It also examines conventional diagnostics and emerging artificial intelligence (AI), molecular, and sensor-based technologies. Current surveillance and biosecurity approaches face challenges in early detection and coordinated response across production settings. AI-enabled monitoring and advanced diagnostics may improve risk assessment, early warning, and outbreak management. However, these technologies require further field validation. Stronger integration of environmental monitoring, data sharing, and established biosecurity practices is needed. A One Health approach can connect animal, human, and environmental surveillance. Such integration may strengthen AIV preparedness and reduce future outbreak risks.

title: Influenza Vaccine Hesitancy and its Associated Factors among Healthcare Workers in Saudi Arabia: A Cross-Sectional Study, 2026
abstract: Background: Seasonal influenza causes substantial morbidity and mortality, and healthcare workers (HCWs) are at increased risk of infection and may facilitate healthcare-associated transmission. Although influenza vaccination is freely available and widely promoted in Saudi Arabia, uptake remains suboptimal. This study assessed influenza vaccine hesitancy and its associated factors among HCWs in Saudi Arabia. Methods: An analytical cross-sectional study was conducted using a self-administered online questionnaire distributed to HCWs across Saudi Arabia. The survey assessed sociodemographic and professional characteristics, vaccination history and intentions, workplace facilitators, perceived barriers, and hesitancy using an adapted 8-item WHO SAGE Vaccine Hesitancy Scale (Cronbach’s alpha=0.91). Hesitancy scores were summarized using the median and interquartile range (IQR). Group differences were examined using Mann–Whitney U and Kruskal–Wallis tests, and a multivariable generalized linear model was used to identify independently associated factors. Results: A total of 395 HCWs participated. Influenza vaccine uptake during the most recent season was 51.4%, and 54.9% intended to vaccinate in the upcoming season. Workplace accessibility and encouragement were reported by 90.1% and 89.9%, respectively. The most common barriers were fear of side effects (33.7%), perceiving influenza as a mild illness (32.2%), and lack of time (28.1%). The median hesitancy score was 32 (IQR 26–37). Profession was associated with hesitancy in the unadjusted analysis (p=0.042). title: The effect of the time of day of influenza vaccination on antibody and T-cell responses in older adults
abstract: Abstract Increasing evidence suggests that time of day of vaccine administration affects immune responses. We aimed to determine the optimal time of day for influenza vaccination by characterising temporal patterns in vaccine-induced immune responses. Additionally, we assessed the effect of vaccination time relative to an individual’s circadian phase on immune responses. A randomised controlled trial was conducted with 278 participants aged 60–85 years, who received influenza vaccination at a randomised time between 09:00 and 17:00. Antigen-specific antibody titers and T-cell responses to three vaccine strains (A/H1N1, A/H3N2 and B/Victoria) were measured pre- and one month post-vaccination. A permutation-based test was used to determine differences in strain-specific immune responses between the three randomisation time blocks (09:00–11:40, 11:40–14:20, 14:20–17:00). As a secondary analysis, strain-specific immune responses were jointly analysed in a single generalised additive mixed-effects model (GAMM) to assess the overall impact of influenza vaccination timing. The permutation-based test found no significant differences in immune responses between the three vaccination time blocks. A GAMM revealed that morning vaccination resulted in significantly higher antibody responses across strains than early afternoon vaccination( p = 0.045), but not late afternoon vaccination ( p = 0.498). Antibody responses displayed a non-significant non-linear pattern from 09:00 to 17:00, with the model suggesting highest responses in participants vaccinated at 09:00. A similar trend was observed for T-cell responses. Irrespective of chronotype, vaccinations administered at the start of an individual’s day tended to elicit the strongest vaccine-induced immune responses. Although statistical evidence for a time-of-day effect was limited, numerically higher antibody and T-cell responses were consistently observed in the morning group.

title: Immunogenicity and safety of two priming doses of an MF59-adjuvanted cell-based H5N8 influenza vaccine in healthy persons aged ≥18 years
abstract: BACKGROUND: Increased transmission of avian influenza from animals to humans has elevated the risk of an H5 pandemic. METHODS: This phase 2, randomized, observer-blind, multi-center trial assessed the immunogenicity and safety of homologous priming with an MF59-adjuvanted, cell-based H5N8 A/Astrakhan/3212/2020 clade 2.3.4.4b vaccine (aH5N8c). We enrolled adults age ≥18 years, equally stratified into 18-64 (including a poultry-worker subset) and ≥65 year cohorts. Primary and secondary outcomes were homologous antibody responses against H5N8 measured in all participants by hemagglutination inhibition (HI) and in a subset by microneutralization (MN) assays on Days 1, 22, and 43. Solicited adverse events (AEs) were monitored for 7 days post-vaccination, with unsolicited AEs tracked throughout Day 43. RESULTS: 239 participants were vaccinated (18-64 years, n = 121; ≥65 years, n = 118). At Day 43 (21 days post second aH5N8c dose), geometric mean fold increases (GMFI) were 13.7 for the 18-64 cohort and 10.2 for the ≥65 cohort. HI seroconversion rates were 75.8% (95% CI 66.1-83.8%) for the 18-64 cohort and 71.0% (61.1-79.6%) for the ≥65 cohort. HI titers ≥1:40 were achieved in 75.8% (66.1-83.8%) and 73.0% (63.2-81.4%) of participants, respectively. MN seroconversion rates were 80.6% (68.6-89.6%) and 70.0% (56.8-81.2%), while MN titers ≥1:40 were 83.9% (72.3-92.0%) and 86.7% (75.4-94.1%), respectively. No notable differences in immune responses by poultry worker status were observed. Most solicited AEs were mild or moderate, resolving within 3 days. Unsolicited AEs were reported by 16.7% participants by Day 43. CONCLUSION: These data support the use of the MF59-adjuvanted, cell-based monovalent H5N8 vaccine as a public health intervention against H5 influenza.

title: The Psychological Impacts of Avian Influenza
abstract: Psychological factors have been neglected in preparation guidelines for an avian influenza (AVI) pandemic. To address this gap, a narrative literature review was conducted to (1) examine how AVI outbreaks—so far largely contained to livestock—have psychologically impacted people, and (2) consider the implications if an AVI pandemic were to emerge, in which large numbers of people would be infected. Findings indicate that AVI outbreaks have been characterized by fear, disgust, and avoidance of poultry products. Many of the other psychological phenomena observed in AVI outbreaks have been documented in past pandemics and other infectious outbreaks: Blame and anger, disease-related avoidance and stigmatization, xenophobia, conspiracy theories, panic buying, and personal stockpiling have all arisen in response to AVI outbreaks. These psychological phenomena may persist and intensify if AVI outbreaks evolve into a pandemic. The lessons learned from COVID-19 can be used to prepare for a possible AVI pandemic. However, additional measures may be needed. Fear, disgust, and avoidance of specific foods would likely distinguish an AVI pandemic from COVID-19. The threat of infected food triggers disgust, and so food-related disgust would likely be a prominent emotional reaction during an AVI pandemic. Public messaging from health authorities and others has the potential to either ease or exacerbate public concerns about food safety, depending on how the messages are crafted.

title: Roost: Avian Influenza Host Genomics Resource
abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) causes mass mortality in poultry and wildlife, and puts already threatened species at further risk. Understanding differences in host susceptibility requires evidence currently scattered across publications, surveillance reports and genomic resources. We present Roost, a web resource that brings together more than 1,300 publications and reports, surveillance detections, and a catalogue of over 2,000 avian genome assemblies. Large language model-assisted literature analysis and comparative genomics link species, genes and molecular mechanisms to their supporting evidence. Around 51% of species with HPAI detections are not represented in the analysed corpus. Research concentrates on poultry, model organisms, and a small set of immune pathways. Research tracks neither mortality magnitude nor extinction risk; species with the largest recorded die-offs and threatened hosts alike remain largely unstudied. Roost makes this evidence, along with genome analyses, accessible to researchers and conservation practitioners, connecting documented disease with host biology and highlighting priorities for sequencing and functional research. Roost is available at http://josephguhlin.com/Roost

title: Emergence of a Distinct Evolutionary Cluster of Clade 2.3.4.4b H5 Viruses in China during 2024-2025 with Rapid Evolution and Antigenic Divergence
abstract: Clade 2.3.4.4b H5 viruses have undergone continuous evolution since their emergence in China, but the extent of genetic and antigenic diversification among recently circulating viruses remains unclear. Here, we characterised 18 H5 viruses isolated through routine surveillance in China during 2024-2025, together with publicly available clade 2.3.4.4b H5 sequences collected since 2020. Phylogenetic analysis revealed that these isolates formed a distinct evolutionary cluster within clade 2.3.4.4b, designated the G2-derived emerging cluster (G2-EC), which emerged around mid-2024 and exhibited clear genetic divergence from previously circulating H5N1 viruses. G2-EC viruses accumulated a characteristic set of hemagglutinin amino acid substitutions, most of which were located in antigenic regions. Across the clade 2.3.4.4b H5 virus population, the estimated mean HA evolutionary rate was higher during 2024-2025 than during preceding periods. These genetic changes were accompanied by marked antigenic divergence from the Re14 vaccine strain, with 4- to 32-fold reductions in HI titres. Genomic analysis revealed acquisition of PB1 segment from a distinct genetic background in G2-EC H5N1 viruses, followed by the emergence of H5N6 viruses sharing a highly similar genetic backbone but carrying a distinct NA segment, indicating sequential reassortment. Animal experiments showed that representative G2-EC viruses retained high pathogenicity and efficient direct-contact transmission in SPF chickens, while exhibiting relatively limited lethality in mice. Collectively, these findings document a recent evolutionary transition of clade 2.3.4.4b H5 viruses in China, characterised by genetic and antigenic divergence accompanied by sequential reassortment, underscoring the need for continued genomic and antigenic surveillance.

source_records.abstract: Clade 2.3.4.4b H5 viruses have undergone continuous evolution since their emergence in China, but the extent of genetic and antigenic diversification among recently circulating viruses remains unclear. Here, we characterised 18 H5 viruses isolated through routine surveillance in China during 2024-2025, together with publicly available clade 2.3.4.4b H5 sequences collected since 2020. Phylogenetic analysis revealed that these isolates formed a distinct evolutionary cluster within clade 2.3.4.4b, designated the G2-derived emerging cluster (G2-EC), which emerged around mid-2024 and exhibited clear genetic divergence from previously circulating H5N1 viruses. G2-EC viruses accumulated a characteristic set of hemagglutinin amino acid substitutions, most of which were located in antigenic regions. Across the clade 2.3.4.4b H5 virus population, the estimated mean HA evolutionary rate was higher during 2024-2025 than during preceding periods. These genetic changes were accompanied by marked antigenic divergence from the Re14 vaccine strain, with 4- to 32-fold reductions in HI titres. Genomic analysis revealed acquisition of PB1 segment from a distinct genetic background in G2-EC H5N1 viruses, followed by the emergence of H5N6 viruses sharing a highly similar genetic backbone but carrying a distinct NA segment, indicating sequential reassortment. Animal experiments showed that representative G2-EC viruses retained high pathogenicity and efficient direct-contact transmission in SPF chickens, while exhibiting relatively limited lethality in mice. Collectively, these findings document a recent evolutionary transition of clade 2.3.4.4b H5 viruses in China, characterised by genetic and antigenic divergence accompanied by sequential reassortment, underscoring the need for continued genomic and antigenic surveillance.

title: Recombinant NDV-vectored vaccine expressing mosaic HA and M2e confers broad and early protection against H9N2 avian influenza virus
abstract: The development of a universal H9N2 avian influenza vaccine is essential to reduce the occurrence of disease and economic losses in the poultry industry. In this study, we developed a recombinant vaccine rTS-mH9-3M2e based on Newcastle disease virus (NDV) avirulent strain TS09-C, containing a chimeric mosaic H9 HA and three copies of H9N2 avian influenza virus (AIV) M2e. The 1-day-old chickens were vaccinated with rTS-mH9-3M2e, which induced broad neutralizing antibody activity against H9N2 AIV, effectively reduced viral load and virus shedding, and reduced clinical signs and tissue damage. Furthermore, rTS-mH9-3M2e can induce cross-neutralizing response to the heterologous subtype AIV H3N2 and conferred cross-protection against H3N2 AIV. When rTS-mH9-3M2e was used as in ovo vaccine, it conferred the earlier protection against NDV and H9N2 AIV compared with post-hatch vaccination. rTS-mH9-3M2e in ovo vaccination significantly increased the level of splenic CD8 + T cells in chickens at 7 days of age and provided 100% protection against H9N2 AIV and 80% protection for NDV virulent strain. These results support that rTS-mH9-3M2e is a promising candidate for development as a broad H9N2 avian influenza vaccine and an in ovo vaccine.

title: Respiratory virus prevalence among healthcare university students in Ecuador: a multicenter cross-sectional study
abstract: Background Respiratory viruses remain a major global public health concern and are among the leading causes of acute respiratory infections worldwide. University students, particularly healthcare students, represent a potentially important group for viral circulation because of frequent social interaction and exposure to clinical environments. Evidence regarding respiratory virus circulation in university populations from Latin America, especially Ecuador, remains limited. Objective To estimate the prevalence of respiratory viruses among 438 healthcare university students in three Ecuadorian cities and to describe the proportion of infections detected in students without symptoms. Methods A multicenter cross-sectional study based on a convenience sample was conducted between January 4 and February 3, 2026, among healthcare university students from universities located in Quito, Guayaquil, and Cuenca, Ecuador. Nasopharyngeal samples were analyzed on site using a combo rapid antigen test for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), Influenza A, Influenza B, and Adenovirus. Sociodemographic and epidemiological variables were recorded. Exact tests and exploratory Firth penalized logistic regression were used to explore factors associated with positivity. Results Fourteen participants tested positive for at least one respiratory virus, corresponding to an overall prevalence of 3.2% (95% CI: 1.8–5.3). Influenza A virus and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) were the most frequent single detections ( n = 4 each), followed by adenovirus ( n = 3). Three coinfections were identified. Eight of the 14 positive participants (57.1%) were asymptomatic, whereas six (42.9%) reported respiratory symptoms. A significant association was identified between symptom presence and viral detection ( p < 0.001). Conclusion Respiratory virus detection among healthcare university students in Ecuador was low, and more than half of the positive students reported no symptoms, suggesting that these viruses may circulate unnoticed within university environments. Because rapid antigen tests have limited sensitivity and do not directly measure infectivity, the true prevalence is probably higher, and studies with molecular confirmation, larger samples, and longer sampling periods are needed. Rapid antigen tests were operationally feasible as point-of-care tools for on-site screening in academic environments.

title: A single-residue deletion in H9N2 hemagglutinin uncouples viral burden from disease severity
abstract: H9N2 avian influenza viruses are characterized by significant genetic diversity. Deletions within the hemagglutinin (HA) receptor-binding domain represent a notable, albeit rare, evolutionary trajectory. Here, we systematically characterized the multifaceted impact of a single-amino-acid deletion at residue 227 of HA (designated HAΔ227), a naturally occurring deletion within the 220-loop that overlaps a key antigenic epitope, using isogenic reverse genetics H9N2 viruses. Paradoxically, the HAΔ227 imposed a fitness cost and was associated with enhanced HA receptor-binding avidity, reduced apparent virion-associated NA activity, altered HA/NA functional balance, attenuated viral replication in vitro, and reduced respiratory shedding in vivo. Notably, despite this compromised replicative fitness, infection with the mutant virus was associated with an altered host immune response in chickens, characterized by elevated levels of interferon-γ (IFN-γ), interleukin-10 (IL-10), interleukin-1β (IL-1β), and monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 (MCP-1). These altered immune responses were associated with more severe pulmonary lesions, indicating a dissociation between disease severity and viral RNA load. Furthermore, the deletion increased the pH threshold for HA-mediated membrane fusion and substantially altered antigenic relationships. Collectively, our findings identify HA residue 227 as a functionally important site at which a single-residue deletion is associated with a phenotypic trade-off between replicative capacity and disease severity: reduced replicative fitness accompanied by altered inflammatory responses and greater tissue injury. This study highlights the potential phenotypic significance of a rare deletion in influenza virus HA and demonstrates that viral burden alone may not adequately predict disease severity.
