title: Seasonal influenza vaccination among healthcare workers in Lebanese hospitals: determinants of uptake post-COVID-19 pandemic and economic crisis
abstract: Background Healthcare workers (HCWs) are at increased risk of acquiring and transmitting influenza. We assessed self-reported influenza vaccination uptake among surveyed HCWs in Lebanese hospitals during 2023–2024, compared it with their reported uptake in pre-pandemic 2018–2019, and identified factors associated with non-vaccination. Methods This cross-sectional survey was conducted from April to July 2024 among HCWs from 14 public and private hospitals across multiple regions of Lebanon. The questionnaire assessed influenza vaccination status, free institutional vaccine provision, awareness, attitudes, and COVID-19 vaccine–related perceptions. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors independently associated with non-vaccination in 2023–2024. Results Among 391 participants, self-reported influenza vaccination uptake was lower in 2023–2024 than in 2018–2019 (29.9% vs 60.5%, p < 0.0001). Free institutional vaccine provision was also lower (39.6% vs 70.1%, p < 0.0001), and 19.2% were willing to pay out of pocket. Higher odds of non-vaccination were observed among HCWs aged <30 years (aOR 3.80, 95% CI 1.96–7.68), non-physicians (aOR 5.17, 95% CI 2.26–12.42), those without free institutional vaccine provision (aOR 17.74, 95% CI 9.38–35.72), those with unfavorable influenza vaccination attitudes (aOR 4.61, 95% CI 2.10–10.63), and those with moderate-to-high COVID-19 vaccine–related hesitancy (aOR 2.09, 95% CI 1.03–4.27). Conclusion Among surveyed HCWs, influenza vaccination uptake in 2023–2024 was substantially lower than reported for 2018–2019. Lack of free institutional vaccine provision and unfavorable vaccine-related perceptions were independently associated with non-vaccination. Restoring free workplace-based vaccination and addressing COVID-19 vaccine–related hesitancy may improve uptake in resource-constrained healthcare settings.

title_zh: 黎巴嫩医院医护人员中的 季节性流感 疫苗接种:COVID-19 大流行和经济危机后的决定因素
source_body_en: Background Healthcare workers (HCWs) are at increased risk of acquiring and transmitting influenza. We assessed self-reported influenza vaccination uptake among surveyed HCWs in Lebanese hospitals during 2023–2024, compared it with their reported uptake in pre-pandemic 2018–2019, and identified factors associated with non-vaccination. Methods This cross-sectional survey was conducted from April to July 2024 among HCWs from 14 public and private hospitals across multiple regions of Lebanon. The questionnaire assessed influenza vaccination status, free institutional vaccine provision, awareness, attitudes, and COVID-19 vaccine–related perceptions. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors independently associated with non-vaccination in 2023–2024. Results Among 391 participants, self-reported influenza vaccination uptake was lower in 2023–2024 than in 2018–2019 (29.9% vs 60.5%, p < 0.0001). Free institutional vaccine provision was also lower (39.6% vs 70.1%, p < 0.0001), and 19.2% were willing to pay out of pocket. Higher odds of non-vaccination were observed among HCWs aged <30 years (aOR 3.80, 95% CI 1.96–7.68), non-physicians (aOR 5.17, 95% CI 2.26–12.42), those without free institutional vaccine provision (aOR 17.74, 95% CI 9.38–35.72), those with unfavorable influenza vaccination attitudes (aOR 4.61, 95% CI 2.10–10.63), and those with moderate-to-high COVID-19 vaccine–related hesitancy (aOR 2.09, 95% CI 1.03–4.27). Conclusion Among surveyed HCWs, influenza vaccination uptake in 2023–2024 was substantially lower than reported for 2018–2019. Lack of free institutional vaccine provision and unfavorable vaccine-related perceptions were independently associated with non-vaccination. Restoring free workplace-based vaccination and addressing COVID-19 vaccine–related hesitancy may improve uptake in resource-constrained healthcare settings.

title: Electrical grounding and directional electromagnetic fields enhance photosynthetic efficiency of Epipremnum aureum (Araceae) and its capacity to reduce influenza A (H1N1) viral RNA in an aqueous leaf-immersion model

source_records.title: Electrical grounding and directional electromagnetic fields enhance photosynthetic efficiency of Epipremnum aureum (Araceae) and its capacity to reduce influenza A (H1N1) viral RNA in an aqueous leaf-immersion model

priority_tier_reason: 补充性记录、预印本或证据完整度有限
full_text: Abstract The application of electrical and electromagnetic approaches to plants has considerable potential for diverse biological and environmental applications. However, whether such approaches can enhance the ability of plants to interact with biological contaminants, including human-pathogenic viruses, remains largely unexplored. This study investigated the effects of electrical grounding and directional electromagnetic fields (EMFs) on the photosynthetic efficiency of Epipremnum aureum and evaluated its potential to reduce detectable influenza A (H1N1) viral RNA using an aqueous viral suspension as a controlled experimental model. Photosynthetic efficiency was assessed by measuring the maximum quantum yield of photosystem II (Fv/Fm) under different electrical treatments. To evaluate changes in viral RNA abundance and distribution, leaves subjected to the corresponding treatments were immersed in an H1N1 viral suspension, and viral RNA was quantified by qRT-PCR in the submerged leaf samples and the surrounding suspension. Electrical grounding combined with a downwardly directed EMF produced the highest Fv/Fm values. In the leaf-immersion assay, the same treatment resulted in the greatest leaf-associated viral RNA recovery and an approximately 96% reduction in detectable viral RNA in the surrounding suspension after 96 h. Photosynthetic efficiency, leaf-associated viral RNA recovery, and viral RNA reduction exhibited similar treatment-dependent patterns, indicating a potential association between plant physiological responses and viral RNA retention and reduction. These findings demonstrate treatment-dependent differences in plant physiological responses and viral RNA retention and reduction within the controlled aqueous leaf-immersion model. Further studies under controlled airborne exposure conditions are required to determine whether these findings can be extended to plant-based biofiltration applications. full_text_excerpt: This study investigated the effects of electrical grounding and directional electromagnetic fields (EMFs) on the photosynthetic efficiency of Epipremnum aureum and evaluated its potential to reduce detectable influenza A (H1N1) viral RNA using an aqueous viral suspension as a controlled experimental model. These findings demonstrate treatment-dependent differences in plant physiological responses and viral RNA retention and reduction within the controlled aqueous leaf-immersion model. Further studies under controlled airborne exposure conditions are required to determine whether these findings can be extended to plant-based biofiltration applications.
